questions.prompt: Which factors influence the effectiveness of instruction tuning?
options: The number of instruction templates used in training.
The tokenization algorithm used by the model.
The diversity of tasks in the fine-tuning dataset.
The order in which tasks are presented during fine-tuning.
accepted: The number of instruction templates used in training.
The diversity of tasks in the fine-tuning dataset.
The order in which tasks are presented during fine-tuning.

questions.prompt: What are key challenges of soft prompts in prompt-based learning?
options: Forward pass with them is computationally inefficient compared to that with hard prompts.
They require additional training, unlike discrete prompts.
They cannot be interpreted or used effectively by non-expert users.
They require specialized architectures that differ from standard transformers.
accepted: They require additional training, unlike discrete prompts.
They cannot be interpreted or used effectively by non-expert users.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the impact of fine-tuning versus prompting in LLMs?
options: Fine-tuning is always superior to prompting in generalization tasks.
Prompting requires gradient updates, while fine-tuning does not.
Fine-tuning modifies the model weights permanently, while prompting does not.
Prompting performs better on in-domain tasks compared to fine-tuning.
accepted: Fine-tuning modifies the model weights permanently, while prompting does not.

questions.prompt: Which of the following aspects of the model outputs are captured by POSIX?
options: Diversity in the responses to intent-preserving prompt variations
Entropy of the distribution of response frequencies
Time required to generate responses for intent-preserving prompt variations
Variance in the log-likelihood of the same response for different input prompt variations
accepted: Diversity in the responses to intent-preserving prompt variations
Entropy of the distribution of response frequencies
Variance in the log-likelihood of the same response for different input prompt variations

questions.prompt: Which key mechanism makes Tree-of-Thought (ToT) prompting more effective than Chain-of-Thought (CoT)?
options: ToT uses reinforcement learning for better generalization.
ToT allows backtracking to explore multiple reasoning paths.
ToT reduces hallucination by using domain-specific heuristics.
ToT eliminates the need for manual prompt engineering.
accepted: ToT allows backtracking to explore multiple reasoning paths.

questions.prompt: What is a key limitation of measuring accuracy alone when evaluating LLMs?
options: Accuracy is always correlated with model size.
Accuracy cannot be measured on open-ended tasks.
Accuracy is independent of the training dataset size.
Accuracy does not account for prompt sensitivity.
accepted: Accuracy does not account for prompt sensitivity.

questions.prompt: Why is instruction tuning not sufficient for aligning large language models?
options: It does not generalize to unseen tasks.
It cannot prevent models from generating undesired responses.
It reduces model performance on downstream tasks.
It makes models less capable of learning from new data.
accepted: It cannot prevent models from generating undesired responses.

questions.prompt: Why is KL divergence minimized in regularized reward maximization?
options: To maximize the probability of generating high-reward responses.
To make training more computationally efficient.
To prevent the amplification of bias in training data.
To ensure models do not diverge too far from the reference model.
accepted: To ensure models do not diverge too far from the reference model.

questions.prompt: What is the primary advantage of using the log-derivative trick in REINFORCE?
options: Reducing data requirements
Expanding the token vocabulary
Simplifying gradient computation
Improving sampling diversity

questions.prompt: Which method combines reward maximization and minimizing KL divergence?
options: REINFORCE
Monte Carlo Approximation
Proximal Policy Optimization
Constitutional AI
